Week 37 Graded Mini Project¶

Conditional GAN (cGAN) for Cats vs Dogs Image Generation¶

Objective¶

In this project, we implement a Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) using TensorFlow.

The model learns to generate images conditioned on class labels:

  • Label 0 → Cat
  • Label 1 → Dog

The workflow includes:

  1. Loading the Cats vs Dogs dataset
  2. Preprocessing images and labels
  3. Building Generator and Discriminator networks
  4. Training the Conditional GAN
  5. Generating and visualizing synthetic cat and dog images

The conditioning mechanism enables the generator to produce images belonging to a specific class instead of generating random images.

In [1]:
# ==========================================================
# Import Required Libraries
# ==========================================================

import tensorflow as tf
import tensorflow_datasets as tfds
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from tensorflow.keras import layers
from tensorflow.keras.models import Model

Dataset Loading¶

In this section we load the Cats vs Dogs dataset using TensorFlow Datasets.

The dataset is split into:

  • 90% Training Data
  • 10% Testing Data

The images and labels are loaded in supervised format where:

  • Image → Input image
  • Label → Class label (0 = Cat, 1 = Dog)
In [2]:
# ==========================================================
# Load Dataset
# ==========================================================

# Split the original training dataset into two parts:
# train[:90%]  -> First 90% of images used for model training
# train[90%:]  -> Remaining 10% of images used for testing/evaluation
# ':90%' means "from the beginning"
# '90%:' means "from 90% until the end"
# Example:
# If dataset contains 23,262 images:
# - Training set ≈ 20,936 images (90%)
# - Test set ≈ 2,326 images (10%)
(ds_train, ds_test), ds_info = tfds.load(
    "cats_vs_dogs",
    split=["train[:90%]", "train[90%:]"],
    shuffle_files=True,
    as_supervised=True,
    with_info=True
)

print("Number of classes:", ds_info.features["label"].num_classes)
print("Training samples:", ds_info.splits["train"].num_examples)

Data Preprocessing¶

Before training the GAN, images must be preprocessed.

The following operations are performed:

  1. Resize images to 64 × 64 pixels
  2. Convert image datatype to float32
  3. Normalize pixel values from [0,255] to [-1,1]
  4. Convert labels into integer format
  5. Create shuffled mini-batches for training

Normalization improves GAN training stability and helps the generator learn efficiently.

In [3]:
# ==========================================================
# Image Preprocessing Function
# ==========================================================

IMG_SIZE = 64
BATCH_SIZE = 64

def preprocess(image, label):
    # Resize image
    image = tf.image.resize(image, (IMG_SIZE, IMG_SIZE))
    # Convert to float32
    image = tf.cast(image, tf.float32)
    # Normalize to [-1,1]
    image = (image / 127.5) - 1
    # Convert label to integer
    label = tf.cast(label, tf.int32)
    return image, label


train_dataset = (
    ds_train
    .map(preprocess, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
    .shuffle(1000)
    .batch(BATCH_SIZE)
    .prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
)

test_dataset = (
    ds_test
    .map(preprocess)
    .batch(BATCH_SIZE)
)

Conditional Generator Network¶

The Generator is responsible for creating synthetic images conditioned on a class label.

Unlike a traditional GAN, the Generator receives both a random noise vector and a class label. This enables the model to generate images belonging to a specific category (Cat or Dog) instead of producing completely random outputs.

Inputs¶

  1. Noise Vector ($z$)

    • Dimension = 100
    • Randomly sampled from a normal distribution

  2. Class Label ($y$)

    • 0 → Cat
    • 1 → Dog

Working Principle¶

The class label is first converted into a dense embedding vector:

$$ e = Embedding(y) $$

The embedding vector is then concatenated with the noise vector:

$$ h = [z ; e] $$

This combined representation contains both:

  • Randomness from the noise vector
  • Class-specific information from the label

The merged vector is projected into a high-dimensional feature space using a Dense layer and reshaped into feature maps of size:

$$ 8 \times 8 \times 256 $$

The Generator then progressively increases the spatial resolution using transposed convolution (Conv2DTranspose) layers:

$$ 8 \times 8 \rightarrow 16 \times 16 \rightarrow 32 \times 32 \rightarrow 64 \times 64 $$

These layers learn to transform abstract feature representations into realistic RGB images.

Output¶

The final layer uses the tanh activation function:

$$ G(z,y)=tanh(x) $$

which produces pixel values in the range:

$$ [-1,1] $$

matching the normalization applied during preprocessing.

The output of the Generator is a synthetic RGB image of size:

$$ 64 \times 64 \times 3 $$

conditioned on the specified class label.

In [6]:
# ==========================================================
# Generator Architecture
# ==========================================================

# Size of random noise vector fed to the generator
LATENT_DIM = 100

# Total number of classes in the dataset
# 0 -> Cat
# 1 -> Dog
NUM_CLASSES = 2


def build_generator():

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Generator Inputs
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Random noise input used to generate new images
    # Shape = (100,)
    noise_input = layers.Input(shape=(LATENT_DIM,))

    # Class label input
    # Shape = (1,)
    # Example:
    # [0] -> Generate Cat
    # [1] -> Generate Dog
    label_input = layers.Input(shape=(1,))

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Label Embedding
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Convert class label into a dense vector representation
    # Cat and Dog labels become learnable feature vectors
    label_embedding = layers.Embedding(
        NUM_CLASSES,
        50
    )(label_input)

    # Flatten embedding output from 2D to 1D vector
    label_embedding = layers.Flatten()(label_embedding)

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Combine Noise + Label Information
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Concatenate noise vector and label embedding
    # This allows image generation to be conditioned
    # on the selected class label
    merged = layers.Concatenate()(
        [noise_input, label_embedding]
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Initial Dense Layer
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Project combined vector into a large feature space
    # Output size = 8 × 8 × 256
    x = layers.Dense(
        8 * 8 * 256,
        use_bias=False
    )(merged)

    # Normalize activations for stable GAN training
    x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)

    # Introduce non-linearity
    x = layers.LeakyReLU()(x)

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Reshape Feature Vector into Feature Maps
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Convert 1D vector into 3D feature map
    # Shape becomes (8, 8, 256)
    x = layers.Reshape((8, 8, 256))(x)

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Upsampling Block 1
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Increase spatial dimensions:
    # 8x8 -> 16x16
    x = layers.Conv2DTranspose(
        filters=128,
        kernel_size=4,
        strides=2,
        padding="same",
        use_bias=False
    )(x)

    x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)
    x = layers.LeakyReLU()(x)

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Upsampling Block 2
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Increase spatial dimensions:
    # 16x16 -> 32x32
    x = layers.Conv2DTranspose(
        filters=64,
        kernel_size=4,
        strides=2,
        padding="same",
        use_bias=False
    )(x)

    x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)
    x = layers.LeakyReLU()(x)

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Final Upsampling Layer
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Generate final RGB image
    #
    # Spatial dimensions:
    # 32x32 -> 64x64
    #
    # Channels:
    # 3 -> RGB
    #
    # tanh activation outputs pixels in range [-1, 1]
    # matching our preprocessing normalization
    output = layers.Conv2DTranspose(
        filters=3,
        kernel_size=4,
        strides=2,
        padding="same",
        activation="tanh"
    )(x)

    # Create Generator model
    return Model(
        [noise_input, label_input],
        output
    )


# Build Generator Network
generator = build_generator()

# Display model architecture summary
generator.summary()

Conditional Discriminator Network¶

The Discriminator determines whether an image is real (from the dataset) or fake (generated by the Generator).

Unlike a standard GAN, the Discriminator also receives the class label associated with the image.

Inputs¶

  1. Image (64 × 64 × 3)
  2. Class Label
    • 0 → Cat
    • 1 → Dog

Working Principle¶

The class label is converted into an embedding vector and reshaped into a spatial label map of size:

$$ 64 \times 64 \times 1 $$

This label map is concatenated with the image, producing a combined tensor that contains both visual information and class information.

The network then extracts hierarchical features using convolutional layers and finally outputs a single value indicating whether the image is real or fake.

Output¶

$$ D(x,y) = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{Real Image} \\ 0 & \text{Fake Image} \end{cases} $$

where:

  • $x$ = image
  • $y$ = class label
In [7]:
# ==========================================================
# Discriminator Architecture
# ==========================================================

def build_discriminator():

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Discriminator Inputs
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Input image of size 64x64 with 3 RGB channels
    # Shape = (64, 64, 3)
    image_input = layers.Input(
        shape=(64, 64, 3)
    )

    # Class label input
    # Shape = (1,)
    #
    # Example:
    # [0] -> Cat
    # [1] -> Dog
    label_input = layers.Input(
        shape=(1,)
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Label Embedding
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Convert label into a learnable embedding vector
    #
    # Embedding dimension = 64 × 64
    # This allows the label to be transformed into
    # a spatial representation compatible with the image
    label_embedding = layers.Embedding(
        NUM_CLASSES,
        64 * 64
    )(label_input)

    # Flatten embedding output into a 1D vector
    label_embedding = layers.Flatten()(
        label_embedding
    )

    # Convert flattened vector into a label map
    #
    # Shape:
    # (4096,) -> (64,64,1)
    #
    # This creates one label value per pixel location
    label_embedding = layers.Reshape(
        (64, 64, 1)
    )(label_embedding)

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Combine Image + Label Information
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Concatenate image and label map along channels
    #
    # Image shape:
    # (64,64,3)
    #
    # Label map shape:
    # (64,64,1)
    #
    # Result:
    # (64,64,4)
    merged = layers.Concatenate()(
        [image_input, label_embedding]
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Convolution Block 1
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Extract low-level visual features
    #
    # Spatial dimensions:
    # 64x64 -> 32x32
    x = layers.Conv2D(
        filters=64,
        kernel_size=4,
        strides=2,
        padding="same"
    )(merged)

    # Introduce non-linearity
    x = layers.LeakyReLU()(x)

    # Dropout helps reduce overfitting
    x = layers.Dropout(0.3)(x)

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Convolution Block 2
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Extract higher-level image features
    #
    # Spatial dimensions:
    # 32x32 -> 16x16
    x = layers.Conv2D(
        filters=128,
        kernel_size=4,
        strides=2,
        padding="same"
    )(x)

    x = layers.LeakyReLU()(x)
    x = layers.Dropout(0.3)(x)

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Classification Layer
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Convert feature maps into a 1D feature vector
    x = layers.Flatten()(x)

    # Produce a single score indicating
    # whether the image is real or fake
    output = layers.Dense(1)(x)

    # Create Discriminator model
    return Model(
        [image_input, label_input],
        output
    )


# Build Discriminator Network
discriminator = build_discriminator()

# Display architecture summary
discriminator.summary()

Loss Functions and Optimizers¶

Training a Conditional GAN involves two competing networks:

  1. Generator
  2. Discriminator

Both networks are trained using Binary Cross Entropy (BCE) loss.

Generator Loss¶

The Generator attempts to fool the Discriminator into believing that generated images are real.

The objective is:

$$ \min_G - \log(D(G(z,y),y)) $$

where:

  • $z$ = random noise vector
  • $y$ = class label
  • $G(z,y)$ = generated image
  • $D(\cdot)$ = discriminator output

A lower Generator loss indicates that generated images are becoming more realistic.

Discriminator Loss¶

The Discriminator learns to distinguish between:

  • Real images from the dataset
  • Fake images produced by the Generator

Its objective is:

$$ \max_D \left[ \log(D(x,y)) + \log(1-D(G(z,y),y)) \right] $$

where:

  • $x$ = real image
  • $y$ = class label

The Discriminator is rewarded for correctly classifying real and fake samples.

Optimizer¶

Both networks use the Adam optimizer:

$$ Learning\ Rate = 0.0002 $$

$$ \beta_1 = 0.5 $$

These hyperparameters are commonly used in GAN training because they provide stable convergence and reduce oscillations during adversarial learning.

In [8]:
# ==========================================================
# Loss Functions
# ==========================================================

# Binary Cross Entropy (BCE) loss is used for both
# Generator and Discriminator.
#
# from_logits=True indicates that the discriminator
# outputs raw scores (logits) instead of probabilities.
cross_entropy = tf.keras.losses.BinaryCrossentropy(
    from_logits=True
)


# ------------------------------------------------------
# Generator Loss
# ------------------------------------------------------
# Goal:
# Encourage the discriminator to classify generated
# images as REAL.
#
# The generator is rewarded when discriminator output
# is close to 1 for fake images.
#
# Target labels:
# 1 -> Real
#
# fake_output:
# Discriminator predictions for generated images
def generator_loss(fake_output):

    return cross_entropy(
        tf.ones_like(fake_output),
        fake_output
    )


# ------------------------------------------------------
# Discriminator Loss
# ------------------------------------------------------
# Goal:
# Correctly classify:
# - Real images as REAL (1)
# - Generated images as FAKE (0)
#
# Total discriminator loss =
# Real Image Loss + Fake Image Loss
def discriminator_loss(
    real_output,
    fake_output
):

    # Loss for real images
    #
    # Real images should be classified as 1
    real_loss = cross_entropy(
        tf.ones_like(real_output),
        real_output
    )

    # Loss for generated images
    #
    # Fake images should be classified as 0
    fake_loss = cross_entropy(
        tf.zeros_like(fake_output),
        fake_output
    )

    # Combined discriminator loss
    return real_loss + fake_loss


# ------------------------------------------------------
# Optimizers
# ------------------------------------------------------
#
# Adam optimizer is commonly used for GAN training.
#
# Learning Rate = 0.0002
# Controls how much weights are updated each step.
#
# beta_1 = 0.5
# Recommended GAN setting that improves training
# stability and reduces oscillations.

generator_optimizer = tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(
    learning_rate=0.0002,
    beta_1=0.5
)

discriminator_optimizer = tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(
    learning_rate=0.0002,
    beta_1=0.5
)

Training Step¶

During each training iteration, both the Generator and Discriminator are updated.

Training Workflow¶

  1. Generate a batch of random noise vectors.
  2. Use the Generator to create synthetic images conditioned on class labels.
  3. Pass real images and generated images through the Discriminator.
  4. Compute Generator and Discriminator losses.
  5. Calculate gradients using automatic differentiation.
  6. Update network parameters using the Adam optimizer.

Gradient Computation¶

TensorFlow's GradientTape records all operations performed during the forward pass.

After computing the losses, gradients are calculated with respect to the trainable parameters of each network:

$$ \nabla_{\theta_G}L_G $$

$$ \nabla_{\theta_D}L_D $$

where:

  • $\theta_G$ = Generator parameters
  • $\theta_D$ = Discriminator parameters

Performance Optimization¶

The @tf.function decorator converts Python code into a TensorFlow computation graph, enabling faster execution and improved training performance.

In [9]:
# ==========================================================
# Training Step
# ==========================================================

# Convert Python function into a TensorFlow graph
# for faster execution during training
@tf.function
def train_step(images, labels):

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Generate Random Noise
    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Determine current batch size dynamically
    batch_size = tf.shape(images)[0]

    # Generate random latent vectors that will be used
    # as input to the Generator
    #
    # Shape:
    # (batch_size, LATENT_DIM)
    noise = tf.random.normal(
        [batch_size, LATENT_DIM]
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Forward Pass
    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Use separate GradientTapes to record operations
    # for Generator and Discriminator independently
    with tf.GradientTape() as gen_tape, \
         tf.GradientTape() as disc_tape:

        # Generate fake images conditioned on labels
        generated_images = generator(
            [noise, labels],
            training=True
        )

        # Discriminator prediction for real images
        real_output = discriminator(
            [images, labels],
            training=True
        )

        # Discriminator prediction for generated images
        fake_output = discriminator(
            [generated_images, labels],
            training=True
        )

        # --------------------------------------------------
        # Compute Generator Loss
        # --------------------------------------------------
        # Generator wants fake images to be classified
        # as REAL by the discriminator.
        gen_loss = generator_loss(
            fake_output
        )

        # --------------------------------------------------
        # Compute Discriminator Loss
        # --------------------------------------------------
        # Discriminator wants:
        # Real images -> REAL (1)
        # Fake images -> FAKE (0)
        disc_loss = discriminator_loss(
            real_output,
            fake_output
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Gradient Calculation
    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Calculate gradients of Generator loss
    # with respect to Generator parameters
    gradients_generator = gen_tape.gradient(
        gen_loss,
        generator.trainable_variables
    )

    # Calculate gradients of Discriminator loss
    # with respect to Discriminator parameters
    gradients_discriminator = disc_tape.gradient(
        disc_loss,
        discriminator.trainable_variables
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Update Generator Weights
    # ------------------------------------------------------
    generator_optimizer.apply_gradients(
        zip(
            gradients_generator,
            generator.trainable_variables
        )
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Update Discriminator Weights
    # ------------------------------------------------------
    discriminator_optimizer.apply_gradients(
        zip(
            gradients_discriminator,
            discriminator.trainable_variables
        )
    )

    # Return losses for monitoring training progress
    return gen_loss, disc_loss

Model Training¶

The Generator and Discriminator are trained alternately for multiple epochs.

An epoch represents one complete pass through the training dataset.

Training Process¶

For each epoch:

  1. Iterate through all training batches.
  2. Execute one training step for each batch.
  3. Generate synthetic images using the Generator.
  4. Evaluate real and generated images using the Discriminator.
  5. Compute Generator and Discriminator losses.
  6. Update network parameters using backpropagation.
  7. Record loss values to monitor training progress.

Epoch Statistics¶

At the end of every epoch, the average Generator and Discriminator losses are calculated:

$$ Generator\ Loss_{avg} = \frac{\sum G_{loss}}{N} $$

$$ Discriminator\ Loss_{avg} = \frac{\sum D_{loss}}{N} $$

where:

  • $N$ = Total number of training batches
  • $G_{loss}$ = Generator loss for a batch
  • $D_{loss}$ = Discriminator loss for a batch

Training Configuration¶

The cGAN is trained for:

$$ 10\ Epochs $$

as required by the project specification.

Monitoring both losses helps assess whether the Generator and Discriminator are learning in a balanced manner throughout training.

In [10]:
# ==========================================================
# Training Loop
# ==========================================================

# Number of complete passes through the training dataset
# Assignment requirement: minimum 10 epochs
EPOCHS = 10

# Iterate through all training epochs
for epoch in range(EPOCHS):

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Initialize Epoch Metrics
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Accumulate generator loss across all batches
    gen_loss_avg = 0

    # Accumulate discriminator loss across all batches
    disc_loss_avg = 0

    # Count total number of processed batches
    steps = 0

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Iterate Through Training Batches
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Each iteration returns:
    # images -> batch of real images
    # labels -> corresponding class labels
    for images, labels in train_dataset:

        # Execute one training step
        #
        # Returns:
        # g_loss -> Generator loss
        # d_loss -> Discriminator loss
        g_loss, d_loss = train_step(
            images,
            labels
        )

        # Add current batch losses to running totals
        gen_loss_avg += g_loss
        disc_loss_avg += d_loss

        # Increment batch counter
        steps += 1

    # ------------------------------------------------------
    # Display Epoch Statistics
    # ------------------------------------------------------

    # Average loss =
    # Total loss across all batches / Number of batches
    print(
        f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{EPOCHS} | "
        f"G Loss: {gen_loss_avg / steps:.4f} | "
        f"D Loss: {disc_loss_avg / steps:.4f}"
    )

Image Generation and Evaluation¶

After training the Conditional GAN, the Generator is used to create new synthetic images.

Generation Process¶

  1. Generate random noise vectors from a normal distribution.
  2. Specify class labels to control the image category.
  3. Pass both inputs to the trained Generator.
  4. Obtain synthetic images conditioned on the selected labels.
  5. Convert pixel values from the normalized range [-1,1] back to [0,1] for visualization.

Label Configuration¶

The following labels are used:

$$ [0,0,0,1,1,1] $$

where:

  • $0 \rightarrow Cat$
  • $1 \rightarrow Dog$

This configuration generates:

  • 3 Cat images
  • 3 Dog images

allowing visual verification that the Generator correctly responds to the provided class labels.

Output¶

The Generator produces:

$$ 6 \times (64 \times 64 \times 3) $$

synthetic RGB images conditioned on the specified labels.

In [11]:
# ==========================================================
# Generate Images
# ==========================================================

# Generate 6 random noise vectors from a normal distribution.
# Shape:
# (6, 100)
#
# Each noise vector acts as a unique latent representation
# that will be transformed into an image by the Generator.
noise = tf.random.normal(
    [6, LATENT_DIM]
)

# Specify labels for conditional image generation.
# 0 -> Cat
# 1 -> Dog
#
# Generate:
# - First 3 images as Cats
# - Next 3 images as Dogs
labels = tf.constant([
    [0],
    [0],
    [0],
    [1],
    [1],
    [1]
])

# Generate synthetic images using the trained Generator.
#
# Inputs:
# - Random noise vectors
# - Corresponding class labels
#
# training=False disables training-specific layers
# such as BatchNormalization updates.
generated_images = generator(
    [noise, labels],
    training=False
)

# Convert generated images from [-1, 1] back to [0, 1]
# for visualization using Matplotlib.
#
# This reverses the normalization applied during
# dataset preprocessing.
generated_images = (
    generated_images + 1
) / 2

Generated Image Visualization¶

The generated images are visualized to evaluate the performance of the Conditional GAN.

Visualization Process¶

  1. Create a figure large enough to display multiple generated images.
  2. Iterate through all generated samples.
  3. Display each generated image.
  4. Assign a title based on the conditioning label:
    • 0 → Generated Cat
    • 1 → Generated Dog
  5. Hide axis values to improve visual clarity.
  6. Arrange images neatly using tight_layout().

Purpose¶

The visualization helps verify whether:

  • The Generator produces visually meaningful images.
  • Generated images correspond to the requested class label.
  • The Conditional GAN has successfully learned class-specific image generation.

Expected Output¶

A grid containing:

$$ 3\ Generated\ Cats $$

and

$$ 3\ Generated\ Dogs $$

generated from random noise vectors conditioned on their respective labels.

In [12]:
# ==========================================================
# Display Generated Images
# ==========================================================

# Create a figure with sufficient space
# to display all generated images
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Iterate through all generated images
for i in range(6):

    # Create a subplot in a 2-row x 3-column grid
    plt.subplot(2, 3, i + 1)

    # Display the generated image
    plt.imshow(generated_images[i])

    # Assign title based on conditioning label
    #
    # 0 -> Cat
    # 1 -> Dog
    if labels[i] == 0:
        plt.title("Generated Cat")
    else:
        plt.title("Generated Dog")

    # Hide axis ticks and labels
    # for cleaner visualization
    plt.axis("off")

# Automatically adjust subplot spacing
plt.tight_layout()

# Render all generated images
plt.show()

Conclusion¶

In this project, a Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) was successfully implemented using TensorFlow to generate class-conditioned images from the Cats vs Dogs dataset.

Key Accomplishments¶

  • Loaded and explored the Cats vs Dogs dataset using TensorFlow Datasets.
  • Preprocessed the dataset by resizing images to 64 × 64 pixels and normalizing pixel values to the [-1, 1] range.
  • Designed a conditional Generator that combines random noise vectors with class label embeddings to generate category-specific images.
  • Built a conditional Discriminator that evaluates image authenticity while considering the associated class labels.
  • Implemented Binary Cross Entropy loss functions and Adam optimizers for adversarial training.
  • Trained the cGAN for 10 epochs using TensorFlow's optimized computation graph (@tf.function).
  • Generated synthetic Cat and Dog images conditioned on user-specified labels.
  • Visualized generated outputs to qualitatively assess image quality and label consistency.

Observations¶

During training, both Generator and Discriminator losses gradually stabilized, indicating that the two networks were learning in a competitive yet balanced manner. The Generator progressively improved its ability to produce images that the Discriminator found increasingly difficult to distinguish from real samples.

Outcome¶

The results demonstrate that conditional information can effectively guide the image generation process. Unlike a traditional GAN, the implemented cGAN successfully incorporates class labels, enabling the generation of category-specific images (Cats or Dogs) from random noise vectors.

Overall, this project provided practical experience in conditional generative modeling, adversarial training, and deep learning-based image synthesis using TensorFlow.
